newsitem.title: UK: Forwarder welcomes Air Canada no-show fines.
newsitem.headline: Forwarder welcomes Air Canada no-show fines.

text.p: Air Canada's initiative in introducing financial penalties against forwarders or shippers who fail to use pre-booked space has been was welcomed by Tony Gray, airfreight director of Swiss-based global forwarder Panalpina in London.
"It will protect average capacity needs and allow the professionals to get the service they need," he said.

"The problem arises when forwarders book space in advance -- just in case -- and then don't use it. We've experienced offloads where other forwarders have not taken up booked space allocations of up to 2-4 tonnes on some flights," Gray said.
The new Air Canada measures could become an industry trend as demand for cargo space intensifies and more airlines adopt similar strategies, he added.
"But we are all dependent on our shippers delivering on time and according to plan....so there has to be a balance in all these measures from all sides," he stated.

Air Canada will impose fines equal to 50 percent of the booked weight at the applicable tariff. The fines will be invoiced through the industry's cargo accounting settlement system (CASS) against forwarders and shippers who fail to use pre-booked capacity on weekend flights from Europe, effective March 1.
Last week in a letter to customers Air Canada's general manager cargo for Europe, Des Vertannes, said:

"The no-show shipment is still a regular occurrence and in certain (European) markets accounts for an average of 16 to 19 percent of total bookings. Although efforts to monitor, identify and take appropriate action have shown some success, it is obvious that more penetrating and dramatic action is needed."
